title: Shipped a full Android game with AI: Claude for code, Gemini for art and music. 1,100 commits, 200k lines, and what broke along the way
author: xxyoshikagekiraxx
selftext:
I just pushed v1.1.28 of **Fish Kingdom**, an aquarium tower-defense game. You feed fish, they drop coins, and you build an army of fish and armed plecos to hold off sea-monster waves. It has a 360-level campaign, 100+ enemies and bosses, 60 weapons, and an online PvP mode. Almost everything was made with AI, so here’s how each part worked.

**Code: Claude Code**

* Vanilla JS with a hand-rolled engine, Pixi for the UI, Capacitor for Android, Supabase for the backend
* About 200k lines, 1,100+ commits and 887 test files. The tests are the only reason it still works. Every feature had to come with a passing test before I accepted it.
* A rules file (CLAUDE.md) made a big difference. Every rule in it exists because the AI did that wrong twice: “gameplay numbers only in Balance.js”, “never hand-draw a fish”, “never trust the client with rewards”.
* The biggest failure was performance. The AI kept “optimizing” my quality system, and mid-range phones lagged three releases in a row. Now the working version is frozen behind tests and only changes with measured data.

**Art: Gemini**

* Sprites are generated on a flat magenta background, then keyed out with Python. Pixels are removed only if they connect to the border, so magenta highlights inside a sprite don’t get holes punched through them.
* Things that went wrong in batch generation:
   * Text captions like “Swim-A” and “Attack” baked into the images. A connected-component cleanup pass fixed this.
   * One enemy drawn facing the wrong way. I added a facing check across all 99 enemies.
   * Duplicate images coming back for different prompts.
   * A white patch on a single frame. Only a full audit of the sprites caught it.
* I generated 147 card backgrounds across several accounts, with a watchdog script that restarts stuck jobs.
* Art got converted PNG → WebP, which cut the app bundle from 149 MB to 91 MB.

**Music and sound**

* Music is Gemini-generated. Combat sounds are a mix of recorded samples and Web Audio synth recipes.

**Trailer**

* Veo clips chained by feeding the last frame of each shot into the next, which keeps the shots continuous. Narration is edge-tts, assembled with ffmpeg.

**What AI still couldn’t do**  
Game feel, balance and Play Store paperwork. The difficulty curve took a dozen retunes based on actual play. Data-safety rejections and ad-network issues took longer than any feature.

The game uses no AI while you play. Everything is baked in.

Free on Android: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.fishkingdom.game](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.fishkingdom.game)

Ask me anything about the pipelines. I’d also love feedback on whether the art reads as consistent.
